text:
maria: Quick question — how do we want the gateway to resolve competing routing signals for canaries? I hit a case where header overrides + user quota shaping both apply.

thomas: We currently prioritize explicit header-based overrides over traffic-split rules. That was the original design so support teams can force a specific model.

lee: That ordering makes sense for emergency debugging, but it breaks our canary metrics. If a header forces 100% to canary, our weighted split telemetry becomes meaningless.

maria: Exactly — customer reported weird spike in errors when support used `X-Model-Variant`. Can't tell if it's canary bug or human override.

anya: Could we make the console show a "policy origin" per request in the traces? e.g., routing: [split: 70/30, override: header, quota: rate-limit-5m] so the timeline clearly shows which policy won.

sam: +1 for policy origin. Also suggest adding a boolean in the rollout UI to "allow manual header overrides" per rollout. Default off for production canaries.

maria: Proposal: precedence order = manual override (if rollout permits) -> quota shaping -> weighted splitter -> fallback. But console should mark overrides and exclude them from canary success rate calc unless explicitly included.

thomas: Implementation note: our current evaluator short-circuits on the first match. Changing to this needs us to evaluate all applicable policies to build the provenance chain. That will add ~3-5ms to gateway path unless we optimize.

lee: We could make the provenance chain computation optional: enabled for tracing samples and for the console's telemetry aggregation job, but not on hot path for every request. Sampling rate wins.

devex-bot: deploy-checklist: remember to add telemetry flag `routing.provenance.sample_rate` and console column for `policy_origin`.

anya: For metrics, we should tag canary requests with `canary_type=explicit_override|split|quota_redirect` so dashboards can filter. Avoid mixing override-driven traffic into A/B results unless someone flips "include_overrides".

sam: UX: in rollouts page show a compact breakdown: 
```
Canary: 10% split
Overrides: 2% (support header)
Quota redirects: 0.5%
Effective test traffic: 7.5%
```

maria: Good. One more: quota enforcement currently happens after routing. That means a request routed to canary might be dropped later by customer quota and then logged as canary error — false positive. We should enforce quota before committing to canary accounting, or at least include quota outcome in provenance.

thomas: Pre-checking quota before routing is tricky for cache efficiency. Maybe mark the request as "candidate" for canary, run quota check, then finalize routing decision. Need to evaluate perf tradeoffs.

lee: Action items: (1) Implement provenance sampling for traces (devex-bot flagged flag), (2) Add tags to metrics (`canary_type`), (3) Console UX toggle to exclude overrides from success calc, (4) Research quota-before-finalize optimization.

maria: I'll open an RFC and a small spike ticket for the quota reorder. tagging @thomas @lee to take spike.

sam: FYI, ops asked that any change to precedence be feature-flagged and behind "rollout.routing-provenance" so we can roll back quickly. :thumbsup:

anya: Thanks everyone — this should make canaries less noisy for product teams.

maria: Closing loop — I'll post RFC link here when ready.
